title: 10-Year Breakeven Inflation Rate
revision_note: FRED publishes T10YIE the same day the underlying Treasury and TIPS constant-maturity yields are quoted; it is not revised after publication.
methodology: Computed by the St. Louis Fed as the 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield (DGS10) minus the 10-year Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) constant-maturity yield (DFII10) at the same tenor.

This is the market-implied average inflation rate over the next ten years, not a forecast and not a survey measure — it reflects what bond prices imply investors expect, which can be affected by liquidity and risk premia as well as by inflation expectations themselves.
notes: Values are percent (2.35 means 2.35%), not a decimal fraction.
No observation is published on weekends or U.S. bond-market holidays; those dates are simply absent, not zero.
FRED labels T10YIE "Copyrighted: Citation Required" (source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis).
